title: Rows, Columns, Sheets & Freeze Panes
goal: Insert and delete rows, hide columns without losing them, auto-fit a squashed column, copy a sheet, and freeze headings so they stay in view while you scroll.

steps.text:
This is a delivery team's week. Look closely: **Wednesday is missing**, so the Total in ==B7== is too low.

Real sheets are never finished. You'll add a row, remove one, hide a column before sharing, and keep headings in view when a list gets long.

We'll start with the missing day, from the keyboard.

steps.prompt:
Excel adds a new row **above** the row you've selected. Wednesday belongs between Tue and Thu, so the new row must appear at row 4.

Click any cell in Thu's row, press [[Shift]] + [[Space]] to select the whole row, then press [[Enter]].
steps.wrongFeedback: Wednesday goes **above** Thu, so Thu's row (row 4) is the one to select. Click a cell in it, then hold Shift and tap Space.
clues: Clicking the number 4 on the left edge selects the row too.
Space is the long bar at the bottom. Shift + Space means “whole row”.

steps.prompt:
Row 4 is selected. Press [[Ctrl]] + [[Shift]] + [[=]] (the **+** key) to insert a blank row above it.

With a whole row selected, Excel inserts at once. With just one cell selected it asks whether to shift cells down or right, so select the row first.

On a Mac, right-click the row number and choose **Insert**.
clues: Hold Ctrl and Shift, then tap the key with = and + on it.

steps.prompt:
Before you insert, look at the Total in `B7`: `=SUM(B2:B6)`.

The new row goes **inside** the list, between Tue and Thu. What will happen to the formula?
steps.explain: When a row goes in **inside** a range, Excel stretches the range, so Wednesday's number will be counted. Insert **below** the last row and the range would not stretch.
wrongFeedback: If that were true, every new row would be silently left out of your totals. Excel stretches the range instead.
`#REF!` appears when you **delete** cells a formula points to, not when you add one.
clues: The new row lands in the middle of `B2:B6`.

steps.prompt:
Row 4 is ready. Click ==A4==, type **Wed**, press [[Tab]], type **22**, then press [[Enter]].

Watch the Total in `B8`.
steps.explain: The Total went from 158 to **180**. The formula had already grown to `=SUM(B2:B7)` when the row went in, so Wednesday's 22 counted the moment you typed it.

wrongFeedback.wrongValue: Row 4 should say **Wed** in column A and **22** in column B. Then the Total in `B8` shows 180.

steps.prompt:
**Pens** was typed twice, so row 3 is a duplicate. You click its row number and press the [[Delete]] key.

What happens?
options: Row 3 disappears and Files moves up
Row 3 is emptied but stays as a blank gap
Excel asks if you want to remove the row
steps.explain: The [[Delete]] key only **clears what's inside**. To remove the row itself, press [[Ctrl]] + [[-]] with the row selected, or right-click the row number and choose **Delete**. Formulas that pointed at removed cells then show `#REF!`.
wrongFeedback: That's what **Delete row** does. The plain Delete key is gentler: it only wipes the contents.
Excel doesn't ask. The key just clears the cells.
clues: Delete (the key) empties cells. Which one removes the row as well?

steps.prompt:
You're sending this price list to a customer, but they shouldn't see **Cost** or **Profit**.

First select both columns: press on the letter ==C== at the top and drag across to ==D==, then press [[Enter]].

Once they're selected, Excel hides them with a right-click and **Hide** (or [[Ctrl]] + [[0]]).
steps.wrongFeedback: Select **both** columns, Cost and Profit: press on the letter C and drag across to D. Leave Price (column B) alone.
clues: Cost is column C and Profit is column D, side by side.

steps.prompt:
You hid columns `C` and `D`, so the letters along the top now read A, B, E…

`B5` holds `=SUM(D2:D4)`, which adds the hidden Profit column. What does `B5` show now?
steps.explain: Hiding only **hides**: every number is still there and still counted. To bring columns back, select the columns on both sides of the gap, right-click and choose **Unhide**.
wrongFeedback: Hidden cells are still in the sheet, and SUM still adds them. Hiding changes what you see, not what is there.
`#REF!` would come from **deleting** column D. Hiding keeps it, so nothing breaks.
clues: Is the Profit data still in the sheet?

steps.prompt:
Column B shows `########`. That's Excel saying the number is too wide for the column, not that your data is lost.

Double-clicking the right edge of a column letter fits it to its contents. The keyboard way: tap [[Alt]], [[H]], [[O]], [[I]] one after another (**Home → Format → AutoFit Column Width**). For row height, the last key is [[A]].

On a Mac, double-click the edge between the column letters.
clues: Alt, then H, then O, then I. Tap and release each.

steps.prompt:
Your workbook has tabs **Jan** and **Feb**. March needs the same layout as Feb, headings and column widths included, and Feb must stay as it is.

What's the cleanest way?
options: Right-click the **Feb** tab, choose **Move or Copy**, tick **Create a copy**
Select every cell in Feb, copy, and paste into a new sheet
steps.explain: A copied tab brings its widths, formats and formulas along. Double-click the new tab to rename it, drag a tab to move it, and [[Shift]] + [[F11]] adds a fresh blank sheet.
wrongFeedback: That renames February's sheet: you'd lose Feb and still have to rebuild it.
That pastes the cells but not the column widths, so you'd redo the layout by hand.
clues: You want a duplicate tab, not a renamed one.

steps.topic: Freeze the header: Alt, W, F, R
steps.prompt:
This list will soon have 500 rows. Scroll down and the headings vanish, and nobody can tell which column is **Fee**. **Freeze Panes** pins rows so they stay in view.

You're in `B5`. Tap [[Alt]], [[W]], [[F]], [[R]] one after another: **View → Freeze Panes → Freeze Top Row**.

A thin line appears under row 1. To undo it, open the same menu: the entry now reads **Unfreeze Panes**.

On a Mac, use **View → Freeze Panes → Freeze Top Row**.
clues: W is for the View tab's Window group, then F for Freeze, then R for top Row.

steps.prompt:
Challenge. This sales sheet will have 300 customers down the side and twelve months across. Scroll either way and you lose the month headings **or** the customer names.

Click the cell you'd select **before** choosing Freeze Panes, so that row 1 **and** column A both stay put. Then press [[Enter]].

(In Excel you'd follow it with [[Alt]], [[W]], [[F]], [[F]].)
steps.wrongFeedback: Freeze Panes pins everything **above and to the left** of the selected cell. Which cell has the heading row above it and the names column to its left?
clues: Not in row 1 and not in column A: it's the first cell of the numbers.
